question: How can something be treated as non-existing even when it is observed as existing?
premises: Something may be observed as existing.
It may nevertheless be treated as non-existing.
This is because it is always apprehended through another factor.
inference: Apprehension through another factor explains treating the observed as non-existing in itself.
plain_english: Even what is seen as existing is treated as non-existing, because it is always apprehended through this.
